text:
maria: Noticed a slow upward memory trend on prod-kv shard-3 starting ~03:45 UTC, APM traces show long-lived sequences. Opening a follow-up thread for action items.
jonathan: copy. Any immediate mitigation?
maria: we rolled a config restart at 04:10 which flattened the slope but didn't eliminate the baseline. no customer-facing errors yet.
lee: uploaded two heap dumps and a timeline trace: gs://redwood/prof/2472101234/dumps.tar.gz. preliminary flamegraph points to persist.encodeBuffer allocations.
nina: tagging in because PCI workloads hit these shards more. we need communication plan if we do short-term evictions.
ops-bot: canary deploy "kv-compact-experiment" started at 2472101400 (shards 3/20).
jonathan: proposed split of work: (A) allocate-source profiling + diff 1) owner @lee 1) due Fri EOD; (B) soft-residency enforcement design 1) owner @jonathan 1) PR proto by Wed; (C) compacting cadence experiments 1) owner @alex 1) canary metrics by Thu; (D) short-term buffer pooling patch 1) owner @sam_k 1) PR tomorrow morning.
lee: initial diff: extra ~30k small objects (32-64 bytes) coming from persist.Encoder.Write -> index/encoder.go:120. Likely ephemeral buffers retained by IndexEntry slices.
maria: sounds like pooling or zero-copy could help. what's the risk for pooling?
sam_k: low-risk path exists: use sync.Pool for index buffers with strict release in hot path. will run microbenchmarks.
jonathan: we should avoid global thresholds. propose percentile-based residency softlimit per shard tied to 99th percentile request seq_len. rollout: canary (1 shard) -> 5% -> 20% -> 100% with rollback criteria (increase in tail latency or OOMs).
alex: compacting cadence: trying `compact_every=5m` on canary. will also add `residency_ratio` gauge and histogram for allocation age. posting dashboards shortly.
lee: flamegraphs: gs://redwood/prof/2472101234/flame.svg. allocating stacks attached to encoder->persist path. also seeing increased fragmentation markers in jemalloc stats.
maria: good catch. fragmentation + lots of small allocs explains steady climb. action: add jemalloc tunables to canary and measure impact. owner @alex, due Thu.
nina: for PCI shards we need a communication template if we trigger evictions. I'll draft a 2-line blurb for support.
jonathan: created tickets RI-2725 (soft-residency per-shard), RI-2726 (buffer-pool patch), RI-2727 (compact-experiment + jemalloc tuning).
ops-bot: RI-2725 assigned to jonathan, due 2027-03-30.
sam_k: opened PR feat/pool-indexbuffers; bench shows ~40% reduction in alloc rate for the encode hot path on local perf harness.
lee: note: if pooling reduces allocs but residency stays high, next step is forced compact + an eviction ramp for low-priority sequences.
maria: scheduling a short sync Fri 09:00 PT to review canary metrics and close action items. will update the incident postmortem with owners/links. please add any additional risks to the sheet: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/def456
jonathan: i'll add perf harness link and the rollback playbook to the soft-residency ticket.
alex: metrics posted: https://grafana.redwood.net/d/kv/compact-experiments?orgId=1&refresh=30s. early signs: fragmentation counters down 8% on canary.
nina: thanks. i'll prepare customer note draft and standby for any eviction-related comms.
maria: thanks team 1) follow-up owners: lee (profiling), jonathan (softlimits), alex (compact+jemalloc), sam_k (pooling), nina (customer comms) 1) next check-in Fri 09:00 PT.
